title: Time-Based Validation Logic
description: Build time-based test logic: validate operation completed within timeout, check if timestamp is recent.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Some operations have deadlines. 'Complete within 5 minutes', 'Timestamp not older than 1 hour'. Build validation logic using DateTime operations and IF statements."
story.context: Time-based validation combines DateTime operations with control flow. Critical for timeout checks, freshness validation, and time-window testing.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Perfect! You validated operations completed on time and timestamps were recent. Time-based logic is essential for production testing."

instructions: Create *** Settings *** section with Library    DateTime
- Log    WARNING: Log is stale (older than 1 hour)
hints: Combine DateTime with IF for conditional logic
Convert To Number for arithmetic comparisons
increment=-30 minutes creates timestamp in past
solution:
*** Settings ***
Library    DateTime

*** Test Cases ***
Validate Operation Timeout
    ${max_duration}=    Set Variable    5
    ${start}=    Get Current Date
    Sleep    1s
    ${end}=    Get Current Date
    ${elapsed}=    Subtract Date From Date    ${end}    ${start}
    ${elapsed_num}=    Convert To Number    ${elapsed}
    Log    Operation took ${elapsed} seconds
    IF    ${elapsed_num} > ${max_duration}
        Fail    Operation exceeded ${max_duration}s timeout!
    ELSE
        Log    Operation completed within timeout
    END

Validate Timestamp Freshness
    ${log_timestamp}=    Get Current Date    increment=-30 minutes
    ${now}=    Get Current Date
    ${age}=    Subtract Date From Date    ${now}    ${log_timestamp}
    ${age_num}=    Convert To Number    ${age}
    ${max_age_seconds}=    Set Variable    3600
    Log    Log is ${age} seconds old
    IF    ${age_num} > ${max_age_seconds}
        Log    WARNING: Log is stale (older than 1 hour)
    ELSE
        Log    Log is fresh (within 1 hour)
    END
    Should Be True    ${age_num} < ${max_age_seconds}

theory.title: Exercise 4.3.5: Time-Based Validation Logic
theory.content:
MENTOR-9: "Real testing isn't just 'did it work?' It's 'did it work FAST ENOUGH?' and 'is this data RECENT ENOUGH?' Time-based validation adds temporal requirements to your tests."

Time-Based Validation Patterns

Timeout Validation:

${start}=    Get Current Date
# ... operation ...
${end}=    Get Current Date
${elapsed}=    Subtract Date From Date    ${end}    ${start}
IF    ${elapsed} > 10
    Fail    Timeout exceeded!
END

Freshness Validation:

${timestamp}=    Get From API    /last_update
${now}=    Get Current Date
${age}=    Subtract Date From Date    ${now}    ${timestamp}
IF    ${age} > 3600
    Log    WARNING: Data is stale
END

Time Window Validation:

${event_time}=    Get From Log
${min_time}=    Add Time To Date    ${now}    -1 hour
${max_time}=    Add Time To Date    ${now}    1 hour
IF    '${event_time}' < '${min_time}' or '${event_time}' > '${max_time}'
    Fail    Event outside valid time window
END

Example: Performance SLA Validation

*** Settings ***
Library    DateTime

*** Test Cases ***
API Response Time SLA
    ${start}=    Get Current Date
    # API call
    ${end}=    Get Current Date
    ${response_time}=    Subtract Date From Date    ${end}    ${start}
    ${rt_num}=    Convert To Number    ${response_time}
    
    # SLA: 95% under 2s, 99% under 5s
    IF    ${rt_num} > 5
        Fail    SLA violated: ${rt_num}s exceeds 5s limit
    ELSE IF    ${rt_num} > 2
        Log    WARNING: Slow response: ${rt_num}s
    ELSE
        Log    Response within SLA: ${rt_num}s
    END

⚠️ Time-Based Validation Tips

  • Always convert to numbers for comparison
  • Use IF/ELSE for conditional behavior
  • Log actual values for debugging
  • Common patterns: timeouts, freshness, windows
  • Combine DateTime with TRY/EXCEPT for retry logic
  • Production tests often have time requirements
